conflict: Configured Hugging Face repository IDs for LoVR, FLARE, LongShOTBench, and VES-Bench do not match the verified release inventory, so actual release snapshots would be rejected or attributed to the wrong repository.
canonical_decision: Use the official release identifiers recorded in dataset_releases.csv: debugger123/LoVR-benchmark; AnonymousFLARE/FLARE; MBZUAI/longshot-bench; buaaplay/VES-Bench. Keep code repositories as separate provenance records.
required_action: Correct the adapter registry and add fixtures/tests for every corrected official identifier before using the adapter for candidate resolution.

conflict: The reproduction audit calls LongShOTBench gated and V-RAGBench gated/terms-controlled, while live release reconnaissance records LongShOTBench as public ungated and V-RAGBench as a public card with no usable payload.
canonical_decision: For the 2026-09-07 package, use the live repository state from dataset_releases.csv, while separately recording upstream media gates and any login or terms encountered. Access state must be re-snapshotted at candidate resolution.
required_action: Revise the reproduction audit and upstream_components rows to distinguish annotation/card access from source-media access and to cite immutable revisions where available.

conflict: The reproduction audit says FLARE and TraceAV licenses were not verified, but the later live reconnaissance records exact card/README license statements and scopes.
canonical_decision: Adopt the later verified statements only for the scopes actually stated: FLARE card metadata says CC BY 4.0 but does not clear Video-MME media; TraceAV says CC BY 4.0 for annotations and accompanying code only.
required_action: Update the audit/component register, preserve the evidence cutoff/access date distinction, and retain unknown_hold for all upstream media rights.

conflict: The release inventory provides several short or file-level revisions while the component register still labels the same releases unpinned; some rows retain mutable main. The architecture requires full immutable repository or dataset commits.
canonical_decision: A candidate may freeze only against a provider-resolved full immutable revision for the exact repository and file set; short SHAs and file revisions are evidence leads, not candidate-freeze revisions.
required_action: Resolve and record full Git/HF commits, distinguish repository revision from file blob revisions, and reject mutable main/latest references.

conflict: The rehearsal plan says the HF reconciliation document is absent and data/hf_recon is empty, although both now exist and contain live checks dated 2026-09-07; the funnel consequently retains stale absence reasons and TBD identifiers.
canonical_decision: Treat the rehearsal plan and funnel as pre-reconciliation drafts. Metadata-only candidate resolution may start only after a versioned reconciliation refresh populates exact release and item fields.
required_action: Update the rehearsal plan provenance statement and replace every stale hf_recon_absent reason/TBD with verified values or an explicit unresolved code; do not infer missing values.

conflict: The plan caps each video at three slots but also says three videos could supply four families each; twelve retained families over three videos is mathematically impossible under the cap.
canonical_decision: A 12-family rehearsal with a maximum of three families per video requires at least four source-disjoint videos. Three videos can be used only if fewer than 12 families are retained or the cap is formally amended.
required_action: Change the plan to require 4-5 videos for a 12-family target and make package validation enforce the cap.

conflict: Stage 3 says media inspection occurs only after Stage 1 permits transfer, but Stage 1 is metadata triage and Stage 2 is the actual rights/access authorization gate.
canonical_decision: No bytes may be acquired or inspected until Stage 2 returns transfer_authorized for the exact asset and rendition.
required_action: Correct the Stage 3 precondition and schedule wording to reference Stage 2/Gate A, then verify all checklists use the same gate sequence.

conflict: The adapter requires a Boolean audio value and defaults video to true; the manifest then writes has_video and has_audio as true and coerces unknown speech/ambient values to false. Most audited releases explicitly have unverified file-level audio, so a snapshot author must invent facts or the candidate cannot be represented.
canonical_decision: Recon must preserve unknown availability as unknown and must not produce an acquisition-manifest media assertion until asset-level verification. False means verified absence, not unknown.
required_action: Introduce a tri-state recon model or a separate release/item record; require verified true video/audio only when drafting an acquisition-gate manifest, and preserve unknown speech/ambient values outside the normative Boolean fields.

conflict: Inspection hard-fails without one complete license object, but several legitimate reconnaissance targets have no license, conflicting licenses, or agreement-based rights. This pressures operators to fabricate a version URL or scope merely to create a candidate.
canonical_decision: Unknown or conflicting license evidence is valid recon data and must remain unknown_hold; it is not a reason to invent a single normalized license. Complete license/grant evidence is required only for later gate approval.
required_action: Make recon license evidence nullable/multi-valued with conflict status; keep manifest drafting fail-closed unless reviewed asset-level evidence is supplied.

conflict: upstream_id can silently fall back to a dataset-local source_id and deduplication compares only the resulting raw string. This cannot reliably detect FLARE/Video-MME, LongVidSearch/LoVR/LongVideoBench, or other cross-release duplicates and may also collide unrelated local IDs.
canonical_decision: Use a canonical upstream identity namespace plus explicit lineage edges; never synthesize an upstream identity from a local row ID. Deduplicate by verified canonical ID, content hash/fingerprint, and reviewed re-upload/excerpt relations.
required_action: Require upstream_namespace and upstream_asset_id or mark identity unresolved; implement lineage-aware cross-dataset dedup and add cross-family tests.

conflict: The plan requires duplicate relationships, but the funnel has no canonical upstream namespace, content hash/fingerprint, parent asset, excerpt, or re-upload relation fields. Known family lineage is only free text.
canonical_decision: Candidate freeze requires an explicit duplicate/lineage table covering FLARE to Video-MME, LongVidSearch to LoVR to LongVideoBench, LongShOT to Video-MME/YouTube, TraceAV to mapped upstream sources, VES-Bench source provenance, and V-RAGBench to Ego4D/EgoLife.
required_action: Add resolvable lineage fields or a referenced dedup ledger and record checked-against scope and disposition for every provisional candidate.

conflict: Six speech/ambient slots are preferentially assigned to sources whose media, audio streams, speech/ambient distinction, or evidence timestamps are unverified; VES-Bench is explicitly vision-focused and LongVidSearch hosts no media.
canonical_decision: The matrix is balanced as a design, not evidence that the 12 candidates can instantiate it. Speech and ambient slots remain feasibility hypotheses until authorized stream/content checks pass; public-source reserves must be available.
required_action: Label slot coverage provisional, define minimum metadata signals for candidate resolution, and pre-plan rights-cleared substitutes for every speech/ambient slot.

conflict: The top-level rehearsal objective requires at least one alternative SES, while the frozen matrix requires alternatives in eight slots. Package-level acceptance also checks only at least one, allowing a package to pass after seven required-alternative slots fail.
canonical_decision: For slot-level freeze, every retained slot marked required_at_least_1_alternative_ses must contain at least two distinct accepted minimal SESs. The at-least-one package statement is only a minimum diversity summary, not a waiver.
required_action: Align the plan and package-level acceptance language with the eight slot obligations and report failures/substitutions per slot.

conflict: The normalized candidate and draft manifest can be built from metadata claims, but an episode requires an acquired content hash, at least two hashed streams, access class, source-time intervals, stream hashes, and transformation IDs. No implemented bridge creates or validates these episode source/evidence objects.
canonical_decision: Metadata candidates may support candidate resolution only. Episode/family creation must wait for an approved manifest, exact acquired bytes, stream probes/hashes, source-time normalization, and transformation provenance.
required_action: Specify and implement a versioned manifest-to-episode source mapping and evidence transformation contract before annotation or family freeze.

conflict: Several mappings are labeled direct or direct-near even though source-time fields, timestamp keys/units, Parquet columns, or joins are explicitly unverified or paper-only.
canonical_decision: Use direct only for inspected serialized fields with pinned evidence. Paper-only concepts, ordinal slices, inferred clip boundaries, and uninspected nested schemas are proposal or blocked mappings.
required_action: Downgrade the affected mapping_status values and require exact field-path/schema fingerprints before candidate freeze.

conflict: The recommended plan calls exact-file fetches and row samples immediate metadata-only actions, while the reproduction checklist defines metadata-only as no dataset shard/large Parquet transfer and prefers server schema/statistics. It is unclear which small data files are authorized by the current package.
canonical_decision: The current package authorizes no network transfer. Candidate resolution may use already present records or separately approved small-text/schema snapshots; any new file transfer requires a distinct metadata-snapshot authorization and allowlist, never media authorization.
required_action: Rename download recommendations as proposed actions, define the approval owner and byte/file allowlist for small metadata, and remove commands that appear executable before that approval.

conflict: The library exports execute_download_plan and will call any supplied ByteTransferBackend after approval, although the document emphasizes that the shipped command performs no transfer. The package therefore contains a transfer-capable programmatic surface.
canonical_decision: No transfer backend is approved or supplied in the current package. Any future backend is a separately reviewed implementation and operational authorization; importing this function is not authorization.
required_action: State this distinction prominently in all plans and add a policy/control preventing backend use in the current preflight package.

conflict: The rehearsal plan says all six named decisions must be allowed for primary public-core use, but the acquisition schema allows derivative, annotation, transcript, and raw-media release to be prohibited or not_applicable at acquisition_approved.
canonical_decision: Acquisition approval and public-core eligibility are separate gates. Public-core candidate freeze requires the specific release decisions demanded by the charter; acquisition_approved alone is insufficient.
required_action: Define and machine-check a rehearsal/public-core gate profile, while compatibility candidates may remain restricted and unpooled under their approved uses.

conflict: The package mixes a normative freeze on 2026-09-05, an evidence cutoff of 2026-09-06, and live verification/preparation on 2026-09-07 without a shared statement of what each date controls.
canonical_decision: 2026-09-05 is the normative design freeze; 2026-09-06 is the claims/evidence cutoff; 2026-09-07 is the live access/inspection and planning date. Later live observations do not silently amend the frozen normative contract.
required_action: Add this date convention to the package index/report and version any substantive normative change through the decision log.

conflict: Recommendations use compound or file-level revisions, mutable main, conditional phrases such as if separately addressable, and files whose exact paths or schema are unverified. They cannot all be executed without resolving or inventing fields.
canonical_decision: A recommendation is actionable only when repository ID, full immutable revision, exact relative path/item ID, expected size/OID, access class, rights status, and output record are explicit. Otherwise it remains a discovery task.
required_action: Split discovery tasks from executable allowlist entries and populate missing fields from immutable metadata snapshots before candidate freeze.

conflict: Every accepted family requires blind complete-source alternative search, but multiple candidate sources are reconstructed clips, annotation-only IDs, unavailable payloads, or mappings to gated media. Current records do not prove that a complete source can be obtained and reviewed.
canonical_decision: Reject or hold any candidate without a verified complete source rendition and stable source-time mapping. Clip-only or annotation-only artifacts may seed triage but cannot satisfy full-source validation.
required_action: Add a complete-source availability and source-time join field to candidate records; hold unresolved candidates before family authoring.

conflict: LongVidSearch has an unresolved 447 versus 444 video count, and V-RAGBench counts and structure are paper/card claims without released IDs or records. Both are still ranked as candidate inputs.
canonical_decision: Use 444 only as the observed distinct-ID count and 447 as the reported count until reconciled; V-RAGBench remains protocol-only and cannot yield candidates until a payload with source IDs and splits is available.
required_action: Block candidate rows from these unresolved populations unless an exact item ID can be resolved from a pinned official payload; preserve claim provenance in the inventory.

conflict: The LoVR fixture uses a different repository namespace, a single CC-BY-4.0 license, invented direct MP4 URLs, transcripts, and explicit audio booleans that contradict or exceed the audited release evidence. Tests therefore prove only synthetic behavior, not compatibility with the real release.
canonical_decision: Fixtures must be explicitly synthetic or be schema-faithful snapshots of the canonical release. They must not be cited as evidence that LoVR provides direct full-video URLs, transcripts, verified audio, or a settled license.
required_action: Add canonical release fixtures with unknown/conflicting states and tests that fail closed on missing audio, unresolved license, and absent direct media URLs.

conflict: The document labels a first real rehearsal and gives post-approval fetch steps, which can be read operationally, while the standing gate decision says real download and annotation are NO-GO and only human Gate A review preparation is authorized.
canonical_decision: The current package may proceed only to metadata-only candidate resolution and human rights/access review preparation. It authorizes neither media download nor content review/annotation.
required_action: Retitle or banner the plan as conditional and non-authorizing; require a new recorded Gate A decision before any media transfer and a separate annotation_approved decision before content annotation.

conflict: The ingestion architecture preserves source_key, release_id, upstream_asset_id, item_id, and raw payload, but the episode source object retains only AV-TRACE asset/manifest IDs and no upstream dataset or item ID. Traceability depends on the external manifest and is not stated as a mandatory referential check.
canonical_decision: The acquisition manifest is the canonical bridge for upstream identity; episode validation must prove that source.asset_id and manifest_revision resolve to a frozen manifest containing the canonical upstream namespace and ID.
required_action: Add an explicit referential-integrity rule and validator test; do not duplicate mutable upstream fields inside episode objects unless the normative schema is versioned.

conflict: The inventory column authorized_acquisition_method contains observed technical routes and upstream commands even where rights remain unresolved, which can be mistaken for an authorization decision.
canonical_decision: Rename this concept to observed_official_access_route or proposed_acquisition_route. The only authoritative acquisition method is the value in an asset-level manifest after the acquisition gate passes.
required_action: Correct the inventory heading and all downstream consumers; retain unknown_hold until named human review records an affirmative authority basis.

conflict: The adapter access_mode vocabulary, release-inventory access_status values, architecture access_gate/media_rights_status fields, and episode access_class are different taxonomies with no specified conversion. A row cannot be propagated without inventing a mapping.
canonical_decision: Keep technical access rights status and episode publication class as orthogonal fields. Define an explicit lossless crosswalk and never derive rights or public-core eligibility from technical accessibility.
required_action: Publish and test the crosswalk before candidate freeze; reject unmapped enum values rather than selecting a nearest label.

conflict: The implemented priority registry has no V-RAGBench, EgoLife, Ego4D, or OmniVideoBench adapter configuration even though the planning and architecture documents depend on those sources; the generic adapters also do not implement the source-family mappings described by the architecture.
canonical_decision: Treat those sources as manual or protocol-only until dedicated configurations and schema-faithful fixtures exist. Do not claim implemented candidate resolution for them.
required_action: Add separate provider/release configurations and source-family normalization tests or explicitly remove them from the executable candidate funnel.
